CASTAWAYProject I14 · Autonomous Environmental Monitoring Vessel

Autonomous watercraft for
lake water-quality monitoring.

A solar-powered autonomous catamaran which can be deployed indefinitely to measure water quality with an array of five sensors and stream data back over cellular.
Ethan Beyer · Harish Eakambaram · Reshial Khan · Robert Kirk · Adam Stelmar
FACULTY Alex Huang  ·  TA Beiqi Li  ·  INDUSTRY Dajon McGill & Danny Bacic · Texas Instruments
01

Problem Definition

Freshwater health depends on factors like pH, turbidity, and temperature, which signal algal blooms, pollution, and ecosystem stress, yet data collection still relies on outdated methods: a person in a boat taking a few samples a couple of times a year.

This approach is costly, sparse, and biased toward accessible areas, leaving large parts of lakes unmeasured and missing critical events like storms or blooms as they begin.

Castaway takes a different approach. It’s a vessel that’s cheap enough to deploy at scale, built to run unattended, and energy-positive so it can stay out for weeks. Instead of occasional sampling, it delivers continuous environmental data.

  • R1
    Mobile, unattended coverage
    full-lake sampling for weeks, energy-positive under typical sun
  • R2
    Sensor accuracy
    ±0.1 pH · ±1 °C · ±5% NTU · ±1 ppt EC
  • R3
    Live telemetry
    <1 s latency · >99% log reliability
  • R4
    Affordable
    far below a commercial moored buoy

02

Platform Specs

  • HULLDual-hull wave-piercing catamaran. 3D-printed shells sealed with an epoxy-laminate skin; 1100 mm × 125 mm pontoons, 8:1 slenderness, plumb bow.
  • DRIVE2× Apisqueen U5 thrusters, max. 180 W, ~15 W cruise. 2–3 kn typical, ~4 kn peak.
  • CPURaspberry Pi Zero 2W running Linux with a custom Rust / tokio daemon; inter-board CAN bus.
  • COMMSQuectel EG25-G LTE with GPS / Galileo / GLONASS. MQTT via HiveMQ Cloud; live video through a Cloudflare Tunnel.
  • POWER960 Wh LiFePO₄ @ 12 V · 100 W solar into 10 A MPPT. ~2 W idle draw.
  • SENSE5-ch water quality: pH, turbidity, temperature, conductivity, sonar depth. + IMU, 9× INA228, motorized depth reel.
03

Design Solution

The design followed three principles to make the system robust, reliable, and extensible. Compute and sensing are split across a CAN bus so each side can evolve on its own. The power system is built around dormancy, so the boat draws very little when it isn’t moving. The software stack is designed to run unattended over cellular, from anywhere.

01 · MODULAR
Compute ↔ Sensing split

Two PCBs connected over a differential CAN bus. The two sides evolve independently. Analog millivolt signals stay local.

02 · POWER
Idle by design

Pi Zero 2 W draws 0.8 to 1.4 W. Nine INA228 sensors sit next to 1 mΩ shunts for clean millivolt measurements. Around 2 W at idle, which translates to roughly 20 days on battery alone.

03 · REMOTE
Rust + HiveMQ + Cloudflare

A Rust tokio daemon publishes MQTT to HiveMQ Cloud. Video streams through a Cloudflare Tunnel. The same code runs in a software-in-the-loop simulator before deployment.

8:1 slender pontoons + plumb bow defeat the 2.5 kn Froude wall on a 1100 mm hull, pushing peak to ~4 kn. Twin-hull geometry also lets Castaway angle perpendicular to wind while station-keeping, limiting drift.
Fig. 2 System architecture: Core Navigation Module ⇌ CAN bus ⇌ Sensor Module over a single 8-pin tether (12 V + CAN).
03.1

Custom Hardware · Wilson & Minnow

WILSON · Core board
Power, compute, comms
WILSON PCB
Pi Zero 2W carrier + integrated power + CAN.
  • Pi Zero 2W carrier · Rust/tokio host
  • 9× INA228 coulomb counters · 1 mΩ shunts
  • MCP2515 + MCP2562 CAN @ 500 kbps
  • DRV8871 reel H-bridge · dual ESC PWM out
  • Quectel EG25-G LTE + GNSS · BNO055 IMU
MINNOW · Sensor board
Submersible water-quality pod
MINNOW PCB
ESP32-S3 CAN endpoint with 5-ch analog front-end.
  • ESP32-S3 · built-in TWAI CAN endpoint
  • 5-ch analog front-end · per-ch power gating
  • pH · turbidity · temperature · conductivity · sonar
  • Local filtering + framing, ships calibrated values
  • Single 8-pin tether: 12 V + CAN to Wilson
03.2

Subsystems

HULL
Wave-piercing catamaran

3D-printed pontoons sealed with an epoxy-laminate skin. 1100 mm × 125 mm slender hulls, plumb bow, solar deck.

POWER
960 Wh LiFePO₄ + 100 W solar

12 V bus, 10 A MPPT, 9× INA228 distributed sensing.

COMPUTE
Pi Zero 2W + Rust daemon

Linux host, tokio async runtime, CAN bus + MQTT.

COMMS
LTE · HiveMQ · Cloudflare

EG25-G modem; MQTT telemetry; Cloudflare Tunnel video.

SENSOR BOARD
Minnow · sensor payload

ESP32-S3 on a 4-layer board, lowered below the hull on an encoded reel. Measures pH, turbidity, temperature, conductivity, and sonar depth through a 5-channel analog front-end with per-channel power gating; ships calibrated frames to Wilson over a single 8-pin tether (12 V + CAN).

▶
Live video + telemetry
Video via Cloudflare Tunnel; telemetry via HiveMQ MQTT
Reachable anywhere
Operate from any browser through cellular NAT

Castaway has been integrated and tested as a full system on open water. Hulls, boards, sensors, cellular link, and dashboard were exercised together, with waypoint navigation, differential-thrust station-keeping, reel-deployed readings, and MQTT telemetry verified end-to-end from shore.

The field runs confirmed the design numbers: a ~2 W idle draw, 100 W of solar covering daily consumption even through overcast, and ~15 W cruise per thruster. Distributed INA228 current sensing gave full energy accountability across battery, solar, motors, and logic in real operating conditions.

Fig. 3 Operator dashboard: live map and telemetry via HiveMQ; live video via Cloudflare Tunnel.
05

Conclusion & Future Work

Castaway turns episodic sampling into continuous environmental telemetry — an energy-positive, CAN-connected platform engineered for multi-week unattended deployments.

Status. Hulls fabricated and open-water tested. Wilson and Minnow boards manufactured, populated, and integrated; full-system validation passing across power, CAN, sensing, and telemetry.

Next. Migrate to a purpose-built embedded MCU for lower idle draw; vacuum-form the hulls for durability; complete a full FMEA and reliability assessment to harden the platform for commercial deployment; and run extended field campaigns to build a rich multi-week dataset across seasons and lakes.
